name: Vex & Ruin PulseHide Rave Coat
description:
An oversized, thigh-length rave coat from street label Vex & Ruin, constructed from layered sound-reactive mesh bonded over a bioluminescent base fabric that pulses between deep violet and acid green in response to bass frequencies. Thousands of micro-LED filaments are hand-sewn into the outer mesh in irregular spiral patterns that bloom outward when the music peaks. The collar is wide and sculptural — stiffened with recycled circuit board resin, raw copper traces still visible. Cut extra-wide at the back with a discrete tail-slit and snap-close panels.

Every coat is numbered on a stamped aluminum tag riveted inside the left cuff. Runs are deliberately small — never more than forty per drop.
functionality: Sound-reactive LED system runs 18 hours on embedded flex-cell battery; tail-slit with snap closure accommodates geneware; wide-back construction fits spinal rigs without bunching.
what_it_says: You know the underground circuit, you found the drop, and you paid what it cost — this coat is a membership card.
price_range: Φ 340 – Φ 520 (secondary market up to Φ 900)
story_hooks: The LED pattern on coat number 31 encodes a location — the wearer has no idea they're carrying an invitation to something that isn't a party.
Vex & Ruin's manufacturer was just bought out by a corponation; the next drop might be the last authentic run before the brand goes corporate.
Two people show up to the same underground event wearing the same number — someone is selling fakes, and Vex & Ruin wants to know who.
